chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, the jurist and compiler of this book, may Allah be pleased with him, said: My father informed me, he said that Sa'd ibn Abdullah informed me, he said that Ahmad ibn Hilal informed me, from Ahmad ibn Salih, from 'Isa ibn Abdullah from the descendants of Umar ibn Ali, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said:

Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, said to Musa ibn Imran: 'O Musa, if the heavens and their inhabitants were in one scale-pan, and the seven earths in the other, and "La ilaha illallah" (There is no god but Allah) in the third, "La ilaha illallah" would outweigh them all.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the weight of saying 'La ilaha illallah' compared to the heavens and earth?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith qudsi underscores the metaphysical weight of *Tawhid* by comparing it against the totality of creation, a theme resonating with Shia emphasis on the centrality of divine unity in spiritual practice. The narration illustrates that the declaration 'La ilaha illallah' possesses an ontological gravity that outweighs the physical universe, reinforcing its role as the key to spiritual reward and divine proximity.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. Muhammad bin Ali bin al-Husayn bin Musa bin Babawayh al-Qummi, the scholar and compiler of this book (ra) said: my father (ra) informed me, he said that Sa'd bin Abdullah said, Ahmad bin Hilal said, from Ahmad bin Salih, from 'Isa bin Abdullah from the descendance of Umar bin Ali, from his father, from Abi Sa'eed al-Khudri, from The Prophet (sw) who said: "

Allah, the Mighty and Sublime told Musa Ibn Imran: O Musa, if the heavens and their inhabitants and the seven Earths were in one side of the scale, and 'Laa ilaaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah) was in the other, 'Laa ilaaha illallah' would outweigh them all."
